text:
sam: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to decide how much of the hosted feature surface we try to emulate in Private/Dedicated via a discovery API vs keeping a thin translation layer. Thoughts?

maria: tl;dr: customers expect parity for core QoS (latency SLOs, fallbacks, billing tags). non-core features can be opt-in.

chris: agree on parity for QoS. but emulating everything (eg streaming semantics + prefix caching + batching hints) in the control plane adds surface area and latency on request path if we aren't careful.

linh: can we push capability discovery to startup/heartbeat instead of per-request? agent announces what it supports once, control plane caches it. reduces runtime checks.

sam: exactly. proposal: a small capabilities schema that agents expose on connect, and a thin per-request header that only contains capability-version and routing-hash. Only control plane does feature mapping.

maria: what about auth differences? hosted uses platform tokens and billing tags, private wants KMS/key material and no token leakage.

chris: we should separate two concerns: capability discovery + operational meta (billing/auth). discovery is read-only and safe to cache. operational meta is tenant-sensitive and must flow per-request.

sam: example capability schema (draft):
```json
{
  "capability_version": "v1",
  "features": ["prefix_cache","streaming_v2","kv_cache_v1","quantized_int8"],
  "max_seq": 4096,
  "batching_modes": ["auto","pin"]
}
```

linh: +1. if we anchor capability_version semantics we can evolve features without breaking older agents. also we can have a compatibility matrix in the control plane.

maria: tradeoff: caching capabilities means control plane might route to a node that advertised a feature but later lost it (OOM/rollback). need heartbeat TTL and quick invalidation hooks.

chris: agree. heartbeat every 30s, TTL 2x heartbeat, and always check concrete runtime for critical ops (eg fallback model existence) before committing a request path that depends on it. non-critical ops can be best-effort.

sam: other big decision: where to implement translation for hosted-only features (eg server-side rerank hooks). Option A: control plane translates into primitive ops for private/dedicated. Option B: provide a sidecar shim in private that implements hosted extensions locally.

maria: option B reduces central complexity and keeps control plane simpler, but we then have to support maintaining the sidecar lifecycle and versioning for customers.

chris: Option A increases coupling and risk of subtle behavior drift (control plane's "translation" may not match on-prem exactness). Operationally heavier though easier to guarantee consistent results for hosted customers.

linh: maybe hybrid: core translations live in control plane (simpler ones: header->flags, routing), heavy user-facing features (rerank, eval hooks) are sidecar plugins. Put plugin API stable surface in RFC.

sam: good hybrid. we also need a fail-open strategy for degraded private nodes: either fallback to hosted (if customer allows egress) or degrade features gracefully (eg no streaming, single-token stepping). define explicit failure modes.

maria: customers will want an explicit config toggle: "allow-egress-fallback": true/false. default false for enterprise. document SLO/behavior per mode.

chris: also need consistent billing tags across environments. suggestion: agent attaches signed usage envelope for private deployments that control plane can verify without seeing raw keys. avoids exposing KMS.

linh: implementation note: use short-lived signed JWTs issued by customer control agent, verify on control plane. store verification keys via existing enterprise KMS integration.

maria: ok action items:
- sam: draft capability schema + versioning rules (owner: sam)
- chris: prototype heartbeat TTL + runtime guard for critical ops (owner: chris)
- linh: design signed usage envelope flow and key rotation notes (owner: linh)
- sam+maria: short doc on egress-fallback policy options + default behavior for enterprise (owners: sam/maria)

sam: thanks — will share a short RFC update with the capability JSON and the hybrid translation model before EOD.

maria: thanks all. small follow-up: include regression test ideas for behavioral parity in the RFC (prompt snippets + metrics).

chris: will add a smoke test harness for streaming vs non-streaming fallbacks.

linh: will mock signed envelope for the prototype.

sam: perfect. closing thread for now unless anyone has objections. :thumbsup:
